questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Import NYC_Film_Permits.txt into Excel. How many records (data rows, not counting the header) does the table have?

fields.label: Number of records

questions.subject: Excel

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many records have a missing value for ZipCode? (Missing values are recorded as N/A.)

fields.label: Records with missing ZipCode
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE ZipCode = 'N/A'

questions.steps: =COUNTIF(N:N,"N/A")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 3

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many records have a ZipCode that is present but invalid (not a five-digit number)?

fields.label: Records with an invalid ZipCode
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE ZipCode <> 'N/A' AND (length(ZipCode) <> 5 OR ZipCode GLOB '*[^0-9]*')

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 4

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which column has the same value for every record? Give the exact column name.

fields.label: Column name
fields.method: SELECT 'EventAgency'

questions.steps: Use a pivot table or =COUNTA(UNIQUE(col)) per column; the one with a single distinct value is constant.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 5

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What are the oldest and newest EnteredOn values? Give the complete date and time.

fields.label: Oldest EnteredOn
fields.method: SELECT MIN(EnteredOn) FROM film

fields.label: Newest EnteredOn
fields.method: SELECT MAX(EnteredOn) FROM film

questions.steps: =MIN(E:E) and =MAX(E:E), formatted as date-time. If the dates are text, the import used the wrong locale.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 6 and 7

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many different event types are there, and which is the most common?

fields.label: Number of event types
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT EventType) FROM film

fields.label: Most common event type
fields.method: SELECT EventType FROM film GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 8 and 9

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Considering only shooting permits: what is the most common Category, and how many shooting permits are in it?

fields.label: Most common category
fields.method: SELECT Category FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Shooting permits in that category
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY Category ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits were granted for student films?

fields.label: Student-film shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Category = 'Student'

questions.steps: =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",K:K,"Student")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 11

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What percentage of shooting permits required approval by more than one Community Board? (A permit lists several boards separated by commas.)

fields.label: Share of shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT AVG(CommunityBoards LIKE '%,%') FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: =COUNTIFS(B:B,"Shooting Permit",I:I,"*,*")/COUNTIF(B:B,"Shooting Permit")

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 12

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: In which year(s) did the number of shooting permits starting in Brooklyn exceed those starting in Manhattan? List every year where this holds.

fields.label: Year(s)
fields.method: SELECT group_concat(y, ', ') FROM (SELECT substr(StartDateTime,1,4) y FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 HAVING SUM(Borough='Brooklyn') > SUM(Borough='Manhattan') ORDER BY 1)

questions.steps: Pivot table: rows = YEAR(StartDateTime), columns = Borough, values = count, filtered to shooting permits.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 13
instructor.note: Brooklyn also exceeds Manhattan in 2018 (176 vs 138), but the data ends on 9 February 2018, so 2018 is a partial year. The key gives 2017 only, which is correct if partial years are excluded. The question does not say so.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What share of shooting permits in Manhattan take place on or near Broadway (BROADWAY appears anywhere in ParkingHeld)? Round to the nearest percent.

fields.label: Share (nearest percent)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(upper(ParkingHeld) LIKE '%BROADWAY%'),2) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Borough='Manhattan'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 14

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many shooting permits entered since 1 January 2013 are for a country other than the United States of America?

fields.label: Foreign shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' AND Country <> 'United States of America' AND EnteredOn >= '2013-01-01'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 15

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is the average duration of a shooting permit in hours? Round to the nearest half hour.

fields.label: Average duration (hours)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG((julianday(EndDateTime)-julianday(StartDateTime))*24)*2)/2 FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: Helper column =(D2-C2)*24, then =MROUND(AVERAGEIF(B:B,"Shooting Permit",helper),0.5).

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 16

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What was the duration of the shortest shooting permit, in minutes?

fields.label: Shortest duration (minutes)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(MIN((julianday(EndDateTime)-julianday(StartDateTime))*24*60)) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 17

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is the average lead time in days between EnteredOn and StartDateTime for shooting permits? Round to the nearest day.

fields.label: Average lead time (days)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(StartDateTime)-julianday(EnteredOn))) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 18

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: On which day of the week do most shooting permits start? Give the full day name.

fields.label: Day of week
fields.method: SELECT CASE strftime('%w',StartDateTime) WHEN '0' THEN 'Sunday' WHEN '1' THEN 'Monday' WHEN '2' THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN '3' THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN '4' THEN 'Thursday' WHEN '5' THEN 'Friday' ELSE 'Saturday' END FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

questions.steps: =TEXT(C2,"dddd") in a helper column, then a pivot table count.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 19

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What percentage of shooting permits include shooting on at least part of a Friday? Round to two decimal places of a percent.

fields.label: Share of shooting permits
fields.method: SELECT AVG(strftime('%w',StartDateTime)='5' OR strftime('%w',EndDateTime)='5' OR (julianday(date(EndDateTime))-julianday(date(StartDateTime))) >= ((5-CAST(strftime('%w',StartDateTime) AS INT)+7)%7)) FROM film WHERE EventType = 'Shooting Permit'

questions.steps: A permit touches a Friday if it starts or ends on one, or spans enough days to pass one: compare the day count with the days from the start weekday to the next Friday.

instructor.source: solutions.xlsx (Excel Part 1 instructor key), question 20

questions.prompt: Split EmployeeCode into Location, EmpID, PlantID and PayPeriod. How many employees work in the USA, and how many of them are paid weekly?

fields.label: Employees in USA
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='USA'

fields.label: …paid weekly
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)='USA' AND substr(EmployeeCode,-1)='W'

questions.steps: Location =LEFT(A2,3); PayPeriod =RIGHT(A2,1); then COUNTIFS.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Create LocationPlantID (for example USA-12). How many distinct LocationPlantID values are there?

fields.label: Distinct LocationPlantID values
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT)) FROM codes2

questions.steps: =LEFT(A2,3)&"-"&MID(A2,FIND("-",A2)+1,LEN(A2)-FIND("-",A2)-1), then =COUNTA(UNIQUE(range)).

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Which LocationPlantID has the most employees, and how many?

fields.label: LocationPlantID
fields.method: SELECT substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT) FROM codes2 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1

fields.label: Employees
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 GROUP BY substr(EmployeeCode,1,3)||'-'||CAST(substr(EmployeeCode, instr(EmployeeCode,'-')+1, length(EmployeeCode)-instr(EmployeeCode,'-')-1) AS INT) ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.prompt: Extract EmpID with MID. What is the sum of all EmpID values, and how many employees have an EmpID above 1500?

fields.label: EmpID above 1500
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM codes2 WHERE CAST(substr(EmployeeCode,4,4) AS INT) > 1500

questions.steps: =VALUE(MID(A2,4,4)). The sum works as a hash total: if any EmpID was extracted wrongly, it will not reconcile.

fields.label: Total Debit

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Do the journal lines balance? Give the sum of the Amount column (debits positive, credits negative).

fields.label: Sum of Amount
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Amount),2) FROM je_lines

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add AccountType with INDEX/MATCH. What is the total Amount on lines whose AccountType is Revenue?

fields.label: Total Amount, Revenue accounts
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Amount),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE a.AccountType LIKE 'Revenue%'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add BusinessUnit to each line. Which business unit has the most journal lines, and how many?

fields.label: Business unit
fields.method: SELECT b.BusinessUnit FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Journal lines
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID GROUP BY b.BusinessUnit ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: PreparerID is only unique together with BusinessUnitID. Add PreparerName using both keys. How many journal lines were prepared by Carolyn Slater?

fields.label: Lines prepared by Carolyn Slater
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE p.PreparerName LIKE 'Carolyn Slater%'

questions.steps: Match on a concatenated key: =INDEX(PreparerInfo!A:A,MATCH(D2&"|"&C2,PreparerInfo!B:B&"|"&PreparerInfo!C:C,0)). A match on PreparerID alone picks the wrong person.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many journal lines have no matching preparer in PreparerInfo (for example lines entered by a subsystem)?

fields.label: Lines without a preparer
fields.method: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE p.PreparerName IS NULL

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add Source to each line. What is the total Debit for lines with Source = CHECK?

fields.label: Total Debit, CHECK
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.Debit<>'' THEN l.Debit END),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE s.Source='CHECK'

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Add GLAccountName. Which GL account has the largest total Debit, and what is that total?

fields.label: GL account name
fields.method: SELECT trim(a.GLAccountName) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE l.Debit<>'' GROUP BY a.GLAccountName ORDER BY SUM(l.Debit) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Total Debit
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Debit),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE l.Debit<>'' GROUP BY a.GLAccountName ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Using AccountClass, what is the total Amount booked to Cash accounts?

fields.label: Total Amount, Cash class
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.Amount),2) FROM je_lines l LEFT JOIN chart_of_accounts a ON a.GLAccountNumber = l.GLAccountNumber LEFT JOIN business_units b ON b.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN preparers p ON p.PreparerID = l.PreparerID AND p.BusinessUnitID = l.BusinessUnitID LEFT JOIN sources s ON s.SourceID = l.SourceID WHERE a.AccountClass='Cash'

fields.label: Rows in 2016 file

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: What is total gross pay for January–June 2015 (Reg_Pay + OT_Pay) and for January–June 2016 (Gross_Wages)?

fields.label: Gross pay 2015

fields.label: Gross pay 2016

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Noah says payroll rose by about $266,000. What is the exact difference in gross pay (2016 minus 2015)?

fields.label: Difference (2016 − 2015)
fields.method: SELECT ROUND((SELECT SUM(Gross_Wages) FROM pay16) - (SELECT SUM((Reg_Pay + OT_Pay)) FROM pay15),2)

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: Extract the three-digit job code from Job (2015) and Project (2016). Which job code has the largest 2016 gross wages, and how much?

fields.label: Job code
fields.method: SELECT CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END FROM pay16 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY SUM(Gross_Wages) DESC LIMIT 1

fields.label: Gross wages 2016
fields.method: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Gross_Wages),2) FROM pay16 GROUP BY CASE WHEN substr(Project,3,1) GLOB '[A-Z]' THEN substr(Project,4,3) ELSE substr(Project,3,3) END ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

questions.steps: =IF(ISNUMBER(VALUE(MID(A2,3,1))),MID(A2,3,3),MID(A2,4,3)) — keep it as text so 001 does not become 1.

questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: For job code 005 (Installation), what were total hours (regular + overtime) in 2015 and in 2016?

fields.label: Hours 2015

questions.prompt: How many 2014 transactions are above the 2014 average transaction amount?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > (SELECT AVG(Amount) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Show the ten vendors with the largest increase in spending from 2013 to 2014 (only vendors used in both years): vendor and difference (two decimals), largest first.
questions.sql:
SELECT Vendor, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Year = 2014 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN Year = 2013 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS DiffSpending
       FROM pcards GROUP BY Vendor HAVING SUM(Year = 2014) > 0 AND SUM(Year = 2013) > 0 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Benford's law: for 2014 transactions of at least $1.00, show each leading digit (1–9) and its share of transactions in percent, rounded to three decimals.
questions.sql:
SELECT SUBSTR(CAST(Amount AS TEXT), 1, 1) AS Digit, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount >= 1), 3)
        FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount >= 1 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Duplicate-payment test: count groups in 2014 with the same cardholder, vendor, TransactionDate and amount occurring more than once (positive amounts only). How many such groups are there?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount > 0
        GROUP BY FullName, Vendor, TransactionDate, Amount HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Round-number test: how many 2014 transactions are four-digit whole-dollar amounts ending in 000 (1000, 2000, … 9000)?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 AND Amount >= 1000 AND Amount < 10000 AND Amount = CAST(Amount AS INT) AND CAST(Amount AS INT) % 1000 = 0

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Which MCC had the largest total 2014 spending, and how much (two decimals)?
questions.sql: SELECT MCC, ROUND(SUM(Amount), 2) FROM pcards WHERE Year = 2014 GROUP BY MCC ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
